Definition: A widely-used loyalty score based on how likely customers are to recommend the company, ranging roughly from -100 (everyone's a detractor) to +100 (everyone's a promoter).
A direct measure of how satisfied customers say they are, usually from a survey rating.
How much effort customers felt they had to put in to get something resolved -- lower effort is generally linked to higher loyalty.
The share of customers who stopped doing business with the company over a period.
The total value a customer is expected to bring over the entire relationship, not just one purchase.
How much, on average, it costs to win one new customer.
The share of prospects or leads that turned into an actual sale.
The share of sales opportunities pursued that were actually won.
The set of sales opportunities currently being worked, not yet won or lost.
Predictable subscription-style revenue, counted on an annual basis.
Predictable subscription-style revenue, counted on a monthly basis.
How much of an assigned sales target has actually been achieved.
The share of customers or users who are still active after a given period.
The number of distinct users who were active at least once in the month.
The number of distinct users who were active on a given day.
The number of customers with an active subscription.
The total time users spend consuming content or using the product.
The share of people who started something (a title, course or level) and finished it.

Also known as: Number of Customers; Active Customers; Total Customers
Definition: The number of customers who bought from or were served by the business in a period.

Also known as: New Customer Count; Customer Acquisitions; Customers Acquired
Definition: The number of customers who bought for the first time in a period.
The number of customers who had bought before and came back in the period.
The number of customers who stopped buying or cancelled in a period.
The money spent to keep existing customers, such as loyalty offers, account management and support.
A combined satisfaction score built from several survey questions, shown on a fixed scale.
How strongly customers prefer to keep buying from the business, shown by repeat purchases and willingness to recommend.
A score that combines usage, support issues, payments and survey feedback to show how likely a customer is to stay.
How hard customers find it to get something done with the business, such as solving a problem. Less effort usually means more loyalty.
The number of complaints received compared with the number of customers or orders, so that busy and quiet periods can be compared.

Also known as: Time to Resolve Complaint; Complaint Closure Time
Definition: The average time taken to close a complaint from when it was received.
The revenue kept from existing customers after upgrades, downgrades and cancellations, compared with what they paid at the start of the period. Above 100% means existing customers are growing.
The share of starting revenue from existing customers that is kept after cancellations and downgrades, ignoring any upgrades.
The share of recurring revenue lost in a period because customers cancelled or paid less.
The share of customers, counted by number rather than by value, who left in a period.
The extra recurring revenue gained from existing customers who bought more or moved to a bigger plan.
The recurring revenue lost from customers who stayed but moved to a smaller plan or bought less.
The average recurring revenue from each customer account.
The profit made from a customer after the cost of serving them has been taken off.
The average length of time a customer keeps buying before leaving.
The time it takes a new customer to get the first real benefit from the product or service.
The share of new customers who finish the set-up steps that lead to proper use of the product.
The share of customers who use a product or feature, compared with those who could.
The number of users who did something meaningful in the product in a period.
The number of different users who were active at least once in a week.

Also known as: Support Tickets; Tickets Raised; Ticket Volume
Definition: The number of requests for help received by the support team in a period.
The number of support tickets that were closed in a period.
The number of support tickets that are still waiting for an answer or a fix.
The average time between a customer raising a request and first getting a reply from the support team.

Also known as: Time to Resolution; Mean Time to Resolve Ticket
Definition: The average time between a ticket being raised and being closed.
The share of customer requests that were solved at the first contact, with no need for follow-up.
The average time an agent spends on a single customer contact, including any follow-up work done straight after.

Also known as: Service Level Agreement Compliance; Calls Answered in Target
Definition: The share of customer contacts answered within the target time, for example calls answered within 20 seconds.
The share of customers who gave up and hung up or left the queue before reaching an agent.

Also known as: Queue Time; Average Speed of Answer; ASA
Definition: The average time customers wait before an agent answers.
The share of an agent's working time spent actually handling customer contacts rather than waiting for them.
The share of support tickets that had to be passed to a more senior team.
The share of closed tickets that the customer reopened because the problem was not really fixed.
The share of tickets or requests that were not handled within the time promised in the service agreement.
The share of new customers who came because an existing customer recommended the business.

Also known as: Average Rating; Star Rating; Customer Rating
Definition: The average score customers give in reviews, usually out of five.
The count of customer reviews received in a period.

Also known as: Feedback Response Rate; Survey Completion Rate
Definition: The share of customers who answered a satisfaction survey out of everyone who was asked.

Also known as: Contract Renewal Rate; Subscription Renewal Rate
Definition: The share of contracts or subscriptions due for renewal that were actually renewed.
The share of subscriptions or orders that were cancelled in a period.

Also known as: Free Trial Conversion; Trial to Paid
Definition: The share of free trial users who went on to become paying customers.
The split of customers into groups with similar needs or behaviour, such as by size, region or spending.
The share of a customer's total spending in a category that goes to this business rather than to competitors.
A way of scoring customers on how recently they bought, how often they buy and how much they spend.
